art_direction: configurator UI on a piping schematic
composition: desktop artboard left, phone artboard right
title block with brand, large caps title and mono subline
eight option tiles in a 3/2/2-style serpentine grid
pipe threads tiles together including a long diagonal
phone: tiles staggered in a zigzag column on the pipe
layout_devices: toggle switch in each tile's top-right
pipe route linking tiles with arrow connectors
motion_implied: toggles flip on and the pipe segment to that tile lights up
tile tags change from selectable to selected
t2i_prompt: Dark navy web section presenting <CONTENT> as a configurator: numbered outline tiles in monospace caps, each with a one-line description and a small toggle switch (steel blue when on, grey when off) and tiny corner tags, arranged in a serpentine grid and threaded together by one glowing double-line steel-blue pipe with arrow connectors and valve symbols. Faint engineering grid with dot matrix. Title block top-left in mono caps. Phone artboard beside it with tiles staggered in a zigzag column. Flat vector UI, square corners, one cool accent.
signature_idea: Options are switches on the actual water train, so choosing one visibly adds it to the pipe.
strengths: makes options feel like engineered modules, not upsells
reuses the diagram language so pages feel related
weaknesses: toggles imply a live configurator that the site does not have
all-mono caps and garbled tags add noise
brand_fit_why: Palette, square tiles and single accent fit; toggles promise interaction the site cannot honour and mono-everything replaces Geist light headlines.
